meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 3: Server Concepts
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: A tools/call reaches your booking tool, which calls an airline API that answers 503. What does a conformant server return?

options.text: A result with resultType input_required, asking the user to retry later
A result with isError: true and text the model can act on
A JSON-RPC error -32603, because the failure happened inside the server
A JSON-RPC error -32602, because the arguments could not be fulfilled

questions.explanation: API failures, validation failures and business-rule failures are tool execution errors: they are reported inside a normal result with isError: true, so the model can self-correct. JSON-RPC errors are for problems with the request itself, such as an unknown tool.

questions.question: A client calls tools/call with name 'serch_flights', a typo. What should the server return?

options.text: A JSON-RPC error -32603 Internal error, since no handler matched
A result with isError: true so the model can retry with a corrected name
A JSON-RPC error -32601 Method not found, since the tool name names the method
A JSON-RPC error -32602 Invalid params: the tool does not exist

questions.explanation: Unknown tool and requests that fail the CallToolRequest schema are protocol errors, reported as -32602. -32601 is for an unknown JSON-RPC method such as tools/cal, not an unknown tool name.

questions.question: A resources/read result carries cacheScope: "private". What does that permit?

options.text: No reuse at all: the response must be re-fetched on every access
Reuse only in memory and never on disk, regardless of which caller the result is served to
Reuse within the same authorization context only, never across different tokens
Reuse by any client, but never storage by a shared gateway or proxy

questions.explanation: private means the response contains data that must not be shared between callers: caches MUST NOT be shared across authorization contexts, so a different access token needs a different cache entry. public means any client or shared proxy may serve it to anyone.

questions.question: A tool declares an outputSchema. What does that oblige each side to do?

options.text: The server MUST return structuredContent conforming to it; clients SHOULD validate it
The server SHOULD validate it, and the client MUST ignore results that fail
The client MUST reject any result that also contains unstructured content blocks
The server MUST return only structuredContent, with no text content at all

questions.explanation: With an output schema, servers MUST provide conforming structured results and clients SHOULD validate them. For backwards compatibility a tool returning structured content should also return the serialized JSON in a text block.

questions.question: Your server ships a prompt template that needs an incident id. How does a client find out the argument exists, and how does it supply one?

options.text: prompts/list declares the arguments; prompts/get is called with values for them
Arguments are declared in server/discover and passed in the request _meta
prompts/get declares the arguments on a first call and accepts them on a second
The client reads the arguments from the prompt text and infers them itself

questions.explanation: prompts/list returns each prompt with its declared arguments, and prompts/get takes the name plus argument values and returns the resulting messages. Nothing about prompt arguments lives in server/discover or in _meta.

questions.question: A client reads file:///reports/q3.pdf, which was deleted. Which response is conformant in 2026-07-28?

options.text: Error -32002 Resource not found, which clients still accept from modern servers
A result whose contents array is empty, letting the client decide what it means
Error -32602 Invalid params, with the uri in error.data
A result with isError: true, since the file's absence is a business condition

questions.explanation: Resource-not-found moved from -32002 to -32602 to align with JSON-RPC. Clients SHOULD still accept -32002 from servers on earlier revisions, but modern servers MUST NOT emit it, and MUST NOT answer with an empty contents array, which is ambiguous.

questions.question: Your client cached tools/list with ttlMs 300000. Two minutes later notifications/tools/list_changed arrives. What should it do?

options.text: Halve the remaining TTL, re-fetching only if the notification repeats
Treat the cached list as stale immediately and re-fetch on next use
Re-fetch immediately and open a new subscriptions/listen stream
Keep the cache until the TTL expires, then re-fetch, since the TTL is authoritative

questions.explanation: TTL and notifications are complementary: a relevant list_changed notification invalidates a cached response even while it is still fresh. The TTL is a freshness hint, not a guarantee and not a polling interval.

questions.question: Your multi-tenant server wants tools/list to differ per caller. What does the spec allow?

options.text: It may vary freely per connection, because each client holds its own session
It may vary only when the server declares listChanged: true in its declared capabilities
It must be identical for every caller, so any filtering belongs in the client
It may vary by the authorization presented, but not per connection or by side effect

questions.explanation: The set MUST NOT vary per-connection or as a side effect of other requests on the connection, but it MAY vary by the authorization on the request, since credentials are per-request input rather than connection state.
